items.question: Why is the fourfold vidyā Ghurghurā honored with salutation?
premises: Ghurghurā is named as a vidyā.
She is renowned by fame.
The speaker bows to this fourfold vidyā.
items.inference: The fourfold vidyā Ghurghurā is worthy of reverent salutation.
items.plain_english: I bow to Ghurghurā, the famous and renowned fourfold vidyā.

items.question: What pleased form of the deity is invoked after the lords of obstacles?
premises: The lords of obstacles are mentioned first.
The deity is then named and pleased.
She has the form of lineage.
items.inference: After the lords of obstacles, the pleased deity in the form of lineage is invoked.
items.plain_english: Then, together with the lords of obstacles, the pleased one, having the form of lineage, is invoked by name.

items.question: Where are these ten mantra-vidyās requested to remain for protection?
premises: Ten mantra-vidyās are addressed.
They are asked to stand or remain.
The specified location is the speaker's head.
items.inference: The ten mantra-vidyās are invoked to remain on the speaker's head.
items.plain_english: May these ten mantra-vidyās stand upon my head.

items.question: Which protective power is asked to stand on the left limb at the time of love?
premises: The left limb is specified.
The time of love is specified.
Śṛṅkhalā is asked to stand there.
items.inference: Śṛṅkhalā is invoked to stand on the left limb at the time of love.
uncertainties: The role of paścime in this context is unclear.
items.plain_english: And at the time of love, may Śṛṅkhalā stand on the left limb, in the west.

items.question: Which powers are invoked to preside in the armor and in the eyes?
premises: Kavacāṅgī is associated with the armor.
Netrakṛtotsavā is associated with the eyes.
Both are invoked together.
items.inference: Kavacāṅgī presides in the armor and Netrakṛtotsavā presides in the eyes.
items.plain_english: May Kavacāṅgī be in the armor, and may Netrakṛtotsavā, who brings delight to the eyes, be in the eyes.

items.question: What role are all the yoginīs asked to perform for the speaker's body?
premises: All yoginīs are addressed.
They are asked to make or constitute something.
The speaker's body and form are the objects.
items.inference: All the yoginīs are invoked to constitute the speaker's body and form.
items.plain_english: May all those yoginīs make my body and my form.

items.question: To whom may this installation of powers be transmitted or withheld?
premises: This śaktinyāsa is the subject.
It is declared not to be given.
The prohibition applies to anyone at all.
items.inference: This installation of powers must not be given to anyone.
items.plain_english: This installation of powers is not to be given to anyone whatsoever.

items.question: What ritual installations are performed by the practitioner addressed as lord?
premises: A practitioner is described as performing rites.
The great installation is named.
The sixfold installation and related rites are included.
items.inference: The practitioner performs the great installation and the sixfold installation and related rites.
items.plain_english: O Lord, one who performs the great installation, the sixfold installation, and so forth.

items.question: What happens to any would-be destroyer after the installation of powers is completed?
premises: The installation of powers has been completed.
A destroyer may arise.
The verb jīvet indicates continued life.
items.inference: Even if a destroyer arises after the installation of powers, that destroyer may live.
uncertainties: The intended force of jīvet in relation to chedakaḥ is ambiguous.
items.plain_english: When the installation of powers has been done, whoever might become a destroyer may live.

items.question: Which section of the tantra is marked by this colophon?
premises: The context is the tantra.
An ordinal number is given.
The term śvāsa marks a section.
items.inference: This marks the fifteenth śvāsa in the tantra.
items.plain_english: In the tantra, this is the fifteenth breath-chapter.

items.question: What is the value of fire offerings, recitations, and elaborate mantra installations by themselves?
premises: Fire offerings are questioned.
Recitations are questioned.
Elaborate mantra installations are questioned.
items.inference: Fire offerings, recitations, and elaborate mantra installations are presented as insufficient by themselves.
items.plain_english: What is the use of fire offerings, what of recitations, and what of elaborate mantra installations?

items.question: What status does the preparatory rite hold in relation to mantras?
premises: Puraskriyā is the subject.
It concerns mantras.
It is called the principal seed.
items.inference: The preparatory rite is declared the principal seed of mantras.
items.plain_english: Indeed, the preparatory rite is called the principal seed of mantras.

items.question: How is a mantra described when it lacks the preparatory rite?
premises: A mantra may lack puraścaraṇa.
The text still declares it a mantra.
The concession is marked by api.
items.inference: Even without the preparatory rite, it is still declared a mantra.
items.plain_english: Even without the preparatory rite, it is still declared to be a mantra.

items.question: Why is the preparatory rite so named in relation to acts of application?
premises: The rite is performed beforehand.
Acts called application follow it.
The ablative gives the reason.
items.inference: It is called puraścaraṇa because it must be performed before acts of application.
items.plain_english: Because it must be performed beforehand for the acts called application.

items.question: How is fruitful service to a mantra compared to service rendered to a king?
premises: Mantra service aims at fruit.
Royal service is given as an analogy.
The comparison is explicit with yathā and tathā.
items.inference: Service to a mantra yields fruit just as service to a king does.
items.plain_english: For the fruit of mantra service, it is just as with service to a king.

items.question: What consequence follows from leaving a mantra unworshipped, and what practice is enjoined?
premises: An unworshipped mantra takes away desires.
This consequence leads to a conclusion.
A triad of practices is enjoined.
items.inference: Because an unworshipped mantra takes away desires, one should practice the triad.
uncertainties: The specific members of the triad are not named in this verse.
items.plain_english: If unworshipped, it takes away desires; therefore one should practice the triad.

items.question: How does worship of the five limbs enable the preparatory practitioner to proceed?
premises: Worship of the five limbs is the means.
The practitioner is a puraścārī.
The result is proceeding happily.
items.inference: By worship of the five limbs alone, the preparatory practitioner may proceed happily.
items.plain_english: Thus, by worship of the five limbs alone, the performer of the preparatory rite may proceed happily.

items.question: What additional practices are named alongside self-consecration for brahmins, O goddess?
premises: Self-consecration is named.
Worship of brahmins is named.
Both are addressed to the goddess.
items.inference: Self-consecration and the worship of brahmins are presented as practices.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, self-consecration and also the worship of brahmins.

items.question: What practice is commonly identified as the preparatory rite in the world?
premises: Worship of the five limbs is named.
The term puraścaraṇa is applied to it.
This identification is said to hold in the world.
items.inference: In the world, worship of the five limbs is called the preparatory rite.
items.plain_english: In the world, worship of the five limbs is called the preparatory rite.

items.question: Which ritual acts are listed as components of the preparatory practice?
premises: Offering to the sun is listed.
Drinking water and bowing are listed.
Worship of the deity is listed.
items.inference: The preparatory practice includes offering to the sun, drinking water, bowing, and worship of the deity.
uncertainties: The syntactic relation of jalapānam to sūryārghya is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Offering to the sun, drinking water, bowing, and worship of the deity.

items.question: What devotional practice performed as a tenth part is called the preparatory rite?
premises: A tenth part is specified.
Worship with devotion is named.
This is called puraścaraṇa.
items.inference: Devotional worship performed as a tenth part is called the preparatory rite.
uncertainties: The token pāsanam may represent upāsanam, but the surface is preserved as given.
items.plain_english: Worship performed with devotion as a tenth part is called the preparatory rite.

items.question: Under what condition does that one remain free from even slight agitation caused by them?
premises: A group of feminine entities is referenced.
Agitation is the potential effect.
The condition is not going to agitation even slightly.
items.inference: The condition described is when that one does not undergo even the slightest agitation from them.
uncertainties: The identity of tāsām and asau is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: When that one does not go to even the slightest agitation because of them.

items.question: What mental steadiness is required of the practitioner's mind in this condition?
premises: The practitioner's mind is the subject.
Agitation is negated.
The negation extends to even slight disturbance.
items.inference: The practitioner's mind must not be agitated in the slightest.
items.plain_english: If the practitioner's mind is not agitated in this way, even slightly.

items.question: Under what repeated condition does that one remain unaffected by even slight agitation from them?
premises: The same condition as before is restated.
A group of feminine entities is referenced.
Even slight agitation is negated.
items.inference: Again, the condition is when that one does not undergo even the slightest agitation from them.
uncertainties: The identity of tāsām and asau remains unspecified in this verse.
items.plain_english: When that one does not go to even the slightest agitation because of them.
